newsitem.title: LATVIA: Second Latvian minister resigns in two days.
newsitem.headline: Second Latvian minister resigns in two days.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele warned on Tuesday that a fresh political crisis could be looming in the Baltic republic after a second minister quit his cabinet in as many days, Radio Latvia reported.

Shkele accepted the resignation of Agriculture Minister Roberts Dilba on Tuesday, who quit after the prosecutor's office accused him of violating anti-corruption legislation by not declaring his stake in two agriculture companies.
Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans was under investigation for similar violations.

Dilba's move followed the Monday resignation of Interior Minister Dainis Turlais, who left his post after eight children plunged to their deaths at a firefighting show on Saturday when the basket they were in fell from a crane.

Shkele, who rushed back from a holiday to head a government commission examining the cause of the tragedy, was quoted by Radio Latvia as saying that a crisis could hit his government if more ministers left their posts.
Political turbulence is common in Latvia, which is governed by an unwieldy seven-party coalition.

Shkele himself quit in fury in January after President Guntis Ulmanis appealed to parliament to reject his choice for finance minister. Shkele returned to office shortly afterwards when he and Ulmanis agreed to bury the political hatchet.
The no-nonsense Shkele, who is an independent, is widely regarded as the only glue binding the government together.
He is credited with ramming a balanced budget for 1997 through parliament and quickening the pace of market reforms, launched when the country left the Soviet Union in 1991.
